criterion_notes.c1: Addresses water supply and sanitation universalization policy and the contractual treatment of favelas and urban peripheries within the 2020-2021 private sanitation concession in Rio de Janeiro, though the primary analytical object is urban-metropolitan planning under fiscal austerity and financialization.
criterion_notes.c2: Both the plain wording and the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2 are satisfied (yes). Under the plain wording, the study examines legal, regulatory, institutional, and governance arrangements shaping the Rio de Janeiro sanitation PPP concession (Federal Law 14.026/2020, the 2017 Fiscal Recovery Plan, and metropolitan governance). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading, beyond macro-financialization discourse, the paper examines specific ownership, tariff, and contractual rules governing service obligations: splitting public wholesale water production (Cedae) from 35-year private retail concessions, wholesale tariff caps and pass-through clauses, omission of non-capital favelas from the tender's baseline registry (Sabren), and Articles 13 and 14 of the Block 01 contract exempting concessionaires from mandatory upgrades in irregular areas unless land regularization, paved streets, drainage, and public security are provided by the state. Nevertheless, under BOTH the plain reading and the narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2, the full-text decision is exclude (E04) because Criterion 4 fails (no realized water or sanitation access outcome is empirically reported).
criterion_notes.c3: Provides empirical documentary, financial, and sociopolitical case-study evidence, including authors' projections of Internal Rates of Return (IRR) from 2020 BNDES pre-feasibility cash-flow data, 2021 auction bid outcomes across four blocks, 2021-April 2023 Siafi-RJ state budget execution of concession fee proceeds, 2020-2022 Cedae operational revenue statements, concession contract clause analysis, and documentation of 2020-2021 public debates in Alerj and civil-society forums.
criterion_notes.c4: Fails Criterion 4: all empirically measured outcomes are financial, fiscal, corporate-revenue, or planning-process outcomes (projected investor IRRs of 25.72%-69.12%, R$24.89 billion in auction concession fees, allocation of only 33% of used state concession proceeds to infrastructure vs. 67% to administrative payroll/operating expenses, and a drop in Cedae's operational revenue from R$6 billion in 2020 to R$2.8 billion two years later). Household or settlement water/sanitation access, connection, continuity, retail tariff affordability, or exclusion under the concession are not empirically observed; universalization shortfalls, retail tariff hikes, and favela exclusion are explicitly framed only as future uncertainties and prospective risks.
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the case-study unit of analysis (Rio de Janeiro state sanitation concession across 4 auction blocks/47 municipalities, public utility Cedae, and state fiscal accounts), exposure (fiscal austerity and financialized PPP concession design/contractual clauses), reported financial/fiscal outcomes, and case-study design, although an empirical service-access outcome is absent.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is written in Portuguese (directly eligible without translation under Criterion 9), with abstracts in Portuguese, Catalan, Spanish, and English.

evidence_quotes.quote: O artigo analisa os efeitos da financeirização urbana e da austeridade fiscal sobre o planejamento urbano-metropolitano, a partir do caso da concessão privada dos serviços de saneamento no estado do Rio de Janeiro (ERJ), Brasil.
Argumenta-se que essa colaboração resulta na captura de rendas públicas no presente, gerando incertezas em relação às promessas de universalização do saneamento no futuro.

Ilustraremos os argumentos a partir de um estudo sobre o desenho da concessão privada dos serviços de saneamento do Estado do Rio de Janeiro (ERJ), Brasil, que ocorreu entre 2020 e 2021. Desenvolvemos referido caso com base em dois grupos principais de fontes e dados.

De acordo com a proposta, a Cedae permanece responsável pela captação, tratamento (produção) e venda de água no atacado para as concessionárias privadas. Estas últimas ficam encarregadas da distribuição e comercialização dos serviços de água e esgotamento sanitário para os consumidores finais.

evidencia que a empresa concessionária não tem obrigatoriedade de investir em aperfeiçoamento do sistema em áreas irregulares, caso não estejam asseguradas condições básicas de regularização fundiária, vias asfaltadas, sistemas de drenagem e presença de segurança pública

A acelerada perda de receita operacional por parte do ERJ inviabiliza o custeio de despesas básicas e compromete os investimentos em infraestrutura urbana. Por outro lado, a crescente demanda por serviços poderá provocar o aumento das tarifas ou, de forma ainda mais grave, a exclusão de assentamentos precários e favelas das metas de cobertura, aprofundando desigualdades preexistentes.

raw_response.exposure: Fiscal austerity (2017 Fiscal Recovery Plan) and financialized 35-year PPP sanitation concession design (privatized retail water/sewerage distribution across 4 blocks with wholesale water supplied by public utility Cedae; wholesale tariff caps; omission of non-capital favelas from tender baseline registry; Block 01 contract Articles 13 and 14 conditioning mandatory concessionaire upgrades in irregular areas on land regularization, paved roads, drainage, and public security)
raw_response.outcome: Financial, fiscal, and planning-governance outcomes: projected investor Internal Rates of Return (25.72% to 69.12%), winning auction concession fees (R$24.89 billion vs. R$10.29 billion minimum), state treasury allocation of concession revenues (33% of R$7.8 billion spent on infrastructure in 2021-April 2023, remainder on administrative operating costs), and Cedae operational revenue decline (from R$6 billion in 2020 to R$2.8 billion two years later); potential effects on water/sanitation coverage, retail tariffs, and favela exclusion are discussed only as future uncertainties/risks
raw_response.population_and_sample: State of Rio de Janeiro (ERJ) and Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Region (RMRJ) sanitation PPP concession covering 47 municipalities across 4 auction blocks (2020-2021 auctions), public water utility Cedae, and state fiscal accounts (2020-2023), with contextual reference to 1,724 ERJ favelas (1,251 in RMRJ) and two 2020-2021 public forums
raw_response.rationale: Excluded under E04 (Wrong outcome). Although Dominguez and Klink (2025) examine the institutional and contractual design of the 2020-2021 Rio de Janeiro private water and sanitation concession—including rule-type contractual clauses (Articles 13 and 14 of Block 01) conditioning concessionaire investment obligations in irregular areas on land tenure regularization, paving, drainage, and public security—the empirical outcomes measured in the paper are exclusively macro-financial, fiscal, and corporate-revenue outcomes (projected investor IRRs, auction concession-fee bids, diversion of 67% of state concession proceeds to administrative expenses, and a 50% drop in Cedae's operational revenue), alongside pre-auction political debates. The paper reports no empirical measurement or observation of realized household or settlement water/sanitation access, connection, reliability, retail affordability, or exclusion under the concession, explicitly framing threats to universalization, tariff increases, and favela exclusion as prospective future uncertainties.
raw_response.study_design: Qualitative and quantitative documentary/financial case study
